title: Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: Arminius's reprobation makes ministers as sluggish — eternal foresight still fixes an immovable decree before the foundation of the world
pass_a_gloss: Further the sentence of Arminius concerning reprobation renders ministers as sluggish as ours. For howsoever he places predestination from foreseen faith, and reprobation from foresight of unbelief, yet he confesses this Divine foresight everlasting, and the same intervening, he acknowledges an everlasting, fixed, and immovable decree, whether of election or of reprobation, established as to singular men before the foundations of the world were laid. A minister therefore cannot hope that by his diligence he can lead unto everlasting life someone thus reprobated from eternity, unless at the same time he believe that he can effect that Divine foresight be deceived, and the everlasting decree of God be revoked. Whether therefore reprobation be placed from the mere liberty of the Divine will, going before all extrinsic causes, or from foresight of unbelief following upon consideration, it is alike: For there will be no one of the hearers but that he is from eternity predestined unto this or that part, from which he will never be transferred unto the contrary part.
pass_b_english: Further: Arminius's view of reprobation makes ministers as sluggish as ours. However he sets predestination from foreseen faith and reprobation from foresight of unbelief, he still confesses that divine foresight eternal — and with it intervening, he acknowledges an eternal, fixed, immovable decree of election or reprobation for each person, set before the world's foundations were laid. So a minister cannot hope by diligence to lead to everlasting life someone thus reprobated from eternity, unless he also believes he can make divine foresight err and revoke God's eternal decree. Whether reprobation is set from mere liberty of divine will before all extrinsic causes, or from foresight of unbelief after consideration, it is the same: no hearer but is from eternity predestined to this side or that, from which he will never be transferred to the other.
source_text: Porro sententia Arminii de reprobatione tam segnes reddit ministros quam nostra. Nam utcunque ille ponat praedestinationem ex praevisa fide, et reprobationem ex praevisione infidelitatis, tamen hanc praevisionem Divinam aeternam fatetur, eademque interveniente, aeternum, fixum, et immobile decretum, sive electionis sive reprobationis, quoad singulos homines ante jacta mundi fundamenta constitutum agnoscit. Minister igitur sperare non potest se aliquem ab aeterno sic reprobatum posse sua diligentia ad vitam aeternam perducere, nisi simul credat posse se efficere ut Divina praescientia fallatur, atque aeternum Dei decretum revocetur. Sive ergo reprobatio ponatur ex mera Divinae voluntatis libertate, omnes causas extrinsecas antegrediente, sive ex praescientia infidelitatis considerationem subsequente, perinde est: Nam nemo erit ex auditoribus, quin sit in hanc vel illam partem ab aeterno praedestinatus, ex qua in contrariam partem nunquam transferetur.
